title: Cain and Abel
lesson: Jealousy left unchecked grows into something terrible. Master it early.
lines: Adam and Eve had two sons, Cain and Abel. Cain grew crops. Abel kept sheep.
Both brought offerings to God. Abel gave the very best of his flock, with all his heart.
Cain brought some of his crops. God looked kindly on Abel's offering, but not on Cain's.
Cain was furious. God warned him: Sin is crouching at your door. You must master it.
But Cain didn't listen. He led Abel into the field. And Abel never came home.
God asked, Where is your brother? Cain said, Am I my brother's keeper? Worst. Alibi. Ever.
Jealousy started small, as a feeling. Left alone, it became a tragedy. Master it while it's small, before it masters you.
Next time: a man builds a giant boat, in the middle of dry land. Follow so you don't miss it!
